correctness.rationale: Orthogonal Laplacian spectral projectors give apex entry (1-f(nh))/n, cross-clique Jensen residual (N+f(nh)-nf(h))/(Nn), and within-clique entry D+(f(h)-f((p_i+1)h))/p_i. Convexity makes D nonnegative and the latter secant correction at least (f(h)-f(nh))/N, so all non-apex entries are nonnegative when the apex entry is. Scalar spectral nonnegativity gives diagonal >=1/n. Conversely an apex edge is negative whenever f(nh)>1. Even Taylor symbols are positive and strictly convex by the explicit Taylor remainder and F_p=F_{p-2}; their beta_p root is unique. The included exact checker passed 3,556 matrices/182,728 entry identities, with finite checks not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full inspected SSP (2001) and positivity-threshold (2005) treatments supply general time-discretization theory but not the explicit sharp scalar apex criterion for every nonnegative convex spectral filter on a heterogeneous clique windmill. The accessible 2014/2015 invariance treatment provides a general polynomial-root framework, not an inspected matching theorem. Kooij (2019) analyzes windmill spectra and graph metrics. Comparison with prior complete multipartite and bipartite graph Taylor results found genuinely different graph hypotheses; stars and complete graphs are acknowledged shared special cases. Priority beyond inspected texts remains unconfirmed.
residual_risks: The complete 2014/2015 specialized polyhedral invariance manuscript could not be retrieved; its abstract is not evidence of whole-paper noncoverage.
The accessible publisher-indexed generalized-windmill text may omit details of spectral applications; no novelty conclusion is inferred solely from this.

Unindexed specialist graph-filter literature or an equivalent theorem in a more general matrix-function setting could establish prior coverage. Independent publication-priority review is not performed.

value.rationale: A structurally motivated exact classification on heterogeneous unions of clique blades yields a one-scalar necessary and sufficient positivity test for an entire cone of nonnegative convex spectral functions, beyond one RK4 graph or a special-case tabulation. It unifies and generalizes the sharp even-order Taylor step across nonbipartite, unequal-blade windmills and identifies permanent apex-driven positivity loss. Exact elementwise preservation is important for nonnegative network diffusion and Markov heat approximations; the stated graph and convexity hypotheses are essential boundaries.
